problem:
Which of the following matrices are symmetric?

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & \sqrt{2} & 7 \\ 0 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,R=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
A square matrix $A$ is symmetric if it is equal to its transpose:

$$
A={A}^{T}
$$

Equivalently, ${a}_{ij}={a}_{ji}$ for all $i,j.$ In other words, $A$ is symmetric across its main diagonal. 

With that in mind, let's examine each matrix in turn.

- $P$ is a symmetric matrix. Indeed, $P={P}^{T}.$

- $Q$ is *not* a symmetric matrix. Since ${q}_{12}\ne {q}_{21},$ we obtain $Q\ne {Q}^{T}.$

$$
Q=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- $R$ is a symmetric matrix. Indeed, $R={R}^{T}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$P$ and $R$ only."
